_note: v18: v15 (= v13's recipe: v9 + 8 LoRA blocks, rank 16) with ONE change: zero-shot v3.6's prompt setup. Each pair (and each disease) gets two sentences, one with the official DPD taxonomic description and one with the short visual symptom description, and its text embedding is the renormalised mean of the two (dpd/prompt_learner.py supports list descriptions for this). v3.6 was the best zero-shot result (HM 11.9% vs v3's 10.2%, seen 10.3% vs 7.8%, unseen disease 18.4%); this tests whether the gain survives training. Compare with v15/v13 on VALIDATION (56.89%); keep only if it beats it by more than 2 points. Costs about twice the text-encoder work per step (666 pair sentences instead of 333).
_result: Not kept. Validation HM 55.6% (epoch 8, gamma 0.075) vs v15's 56.89%: -1.3 points, inside the ~3-point noise and not above the 2-point margin, so v3.6's two-sentence prompts do not improve the trained recipe. Test (for the record only, not used to decide): seen top-1 56.7% (v15 52.2%), unseen 80.3% (v15 84.3%), HM 66.5% top-1 / 92.4% top-5 (v15 64.5% / 92.1%). Same pattern as the zero-shot study: the taxonomy text shifts accuracy from unseen to seen; disease transfer at gamma 0 on validation 9.9% vs 9.2%. v19 (v18 + CNN v2) was skipped because the CNN v2 run crashed (Windows error 1455) in its final refit.

model._note: Same OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16 (QuickGELU) as v5/v6; the text encoder stays frozen.

image_encoder._note: From v13: v9 + more LoRA capacity: last 8 blocks instead of 4, rank 16 instead of 8. alpha 16 -> 32 keeps the LoRA scale (alpha/rank) at 2, so only capacity changes, not the effective step size. About 4x more adapter parameters (1.57M vs 393k). Same lr.

input._note: Images come from the 256 px resize cache (runs/cache/resized_256, shared with the CNN baselines). Test: CLIP's resize 224 + centre crop + CLIP mean/std. The app must standardise uploads the same way (dpd/resize_cache.standardise).

augmentation._note: Same as the CNN baselines except a milder crop scale (0.5-1 instead of 0.25-1), because CLIP's pretrained features expect whole-object views. No hue jitter: colour is diagnostic.

prompts._note: Same templates as v15; descriptions_file changed to v3.6's [taxonomy, visual] lists, so every pair and disease sentence is filled once with each and averaged. Inherits the official DPD descriptions' licence caveat.

validation._note: Same procedure as v6 but 1 split instead of 3: each split is now a full training run with the image encoder in the loop (images instead of cached embeddings). Note v6 showed one split can mis-set gamma, so treat v9's gamma with that caveat.

training._note: Prompt vectors as v6 (AdamW lr 2e-4, weight decay 0, logit scale 100, loss weights pair 1 / crop 0.5 / disease 0.5). max_epochs 30 -> 15 (v5/v6 selected epochs 13-18 with cached features; each epoch now re-encodes every image). Batch 256 -> 64 for GPU memory with gradients through 4 image-encoder blocks.

runtime._note: Gradient checkpointing on the text encoder as before. 4 dataloader workers read the resize cache.
